title: Health, metrics, logs and alerts
summary: Know it is healthy, see how it performs, find what failed, and avoid the dashboard that always says zero failures.

steps.title: Health and metrics
body: Three questions every day: **is it healthy? how is it performing? what exactly failed?**
- **Health** endpoints (`/q/health`, `/health`; liveness and readiness): status up/down with checks for the Camel
context and each route. Containers, Kubernetes and load balancers call them to decide whether to send traffic or
restart. ASP.NET Core's `MapHealthChecks` is the same idea.
- **Metrics** (Prometheus format): counters such as total, succeeded and failed exchanges per route, plus timings.
Prometheus scrapes them, Grafana draws them, alert rules fire on them. The gateway has its own analytics
(calls per API, per application, per status code).

steps.prompt: A route's dashboard shows **0 failed exchanges** all week, yet consumers received hundreds of 400, 404, 502 and 504 responses. Why?
options: The error handler handles every failure, and a handled exchange counts as succeeded; count the error route's exchanges or the HTTP status codes instead
steps.explain: This is the "zero failures" trap. A metric that counts *unhandled* exceptions measures how good your error handler is, not how healthy the service is.

steps.title: Logs with trace ids
body: A log line is only useful if you can **find** it. Put the trace id on every line, and keep secrets and personal
Ship logs from every container to one place (Fluent Bit or a similar agent into OpenSearch, Elastic, Loki,
Application Insights), so a search for `9b01aa3e` covers the gateway, every integration and the backends, for
every day, not just one container's console. Never log tokens, secrets or full request bodies with personal data.

steps.prompt: Which metric best tells you consumers are being hurt?
options: The rate of 5xx responses (and latency) per API at the gateway, compared with the total
The count of failed exchanges in a route that handles all errors
steps.explain: Measure what consumers experience: status codes and latency at the edge. Internal counters are for diagnosis.

steps.title: Metrics that count correctly
prompt: - `void Record(string route, int status, int latencyMs)`: one request outcome;
- `string Snapshot(string route)`: `"total={n} ok={2xx/3xx} client_errors={4xx} server_errors={5xx} p95={ms}"` for that route (`p95=0` with no data);
- p95: sort the latencies ascending and take the element at index `ceil(0.95 × count) − 1` (the nearest-rank method);
- `double ErrorRate(string route)`: server errors ÷ total (`0` with no data). 4xx are the consumer's errors and don't count here.
starter: public void Record(string route, int status, int latencyMs) { }
solution: readonly Dictionary<string, List<(int Status, int Latency)>> data = new();
public void Record(string route, int status, int latencyMs)
if (!data.TryGetValue(route, out var list)) data[route] = list = new();
return list is null || list.Count == 0 ? 0 : (double)list.Count(x => x.Status >= 500) / list.Count;
template: for (int i = 0; i < dojoLat.Length; i++) dojoM.Record("get-book", dojoSt[i], dojoLat[i]);
Dojo.Eq("get-book snapshot", "total=20 ok=16 client_errors=2 server_errors=2 p95=2900", dojoM.Snapshot("get-book"));
Dojo.Eq("routes are separate", "total=1 ok=1 client_errors=0 server_errors=0 p95=80", dojoM.Snapshot("create-order"));
Dojo.Eq("no data", "total=0 ok=0 client_errors=0 server_errors=0 p95=0", dojoM.Snapshot("nothing"));

steps.title: Find the journey of one request
prompt: Support has a trace id. Log lines from several services look like
Write `(List<string> Journey, string? FirstError) Investigate(IEnumerable<string> lines, string traceId)`:
- `Journey`: the lines containing exactly `[traceId]`, sorted by timestamp (the timestamps are ISO-8601, so ordinal string order works), formatted as `"{service}: {message}"`;
- `FirstError`: the earliest `ERROR` line of that journey in the same format, or null.
- Ignore malformed lines (fewer than 5 space-separated parts, or a third part not in `[...]`).
starter: (List<string> Journey, string? FirstError) Investigate(IEnumerable<string> lines, string traceId)
solution: (List<string> Journey, string? FirstError) Investigate(IEnumerable<string> lines, string traceId)
